correction: Use the correctly labelled2021-base index levels. The official January2025 historical table reports2019 annual90.2 and2023 annual126.1. Their independently calculated change is(126.1/90.2-1)*100=39.8004%, close to40%. Different within-year endpoints may exceed40%; no separate false-growth finding is made.
effect: Corrects index-level/base reporting. It does not materially remove the evidence of substantial construction-price increases or the general case for discussing indexation.
limits: Ancillary minor issue. A rescaling or clerical mistake is a strong benign explanation, and the implied relative movement remains approximately right. The author does not specify particular months or an annual-average definition, so the precise wording about growth above40% is not separately adjudicated. Construction prices do not alone decide the appropriate threshold, but this screen does not determine whether doubling it or indexing it is justified. No intent is inferred.
materiality_explanation: Minor: wrong reported index levels and base, with little practical change to the approximately40%growth premise. This should not be presented as a major inflation exaggeration or a refutation of the policy request.
direction_explanation: Null: both levels move downward under correction while their ratio remains similar. A definite favourable effect on the indexation request is not established.

The initial historical Destatis publication retrieved in follow-up is the November2022 release, revised10May2023, not a2023index-year release. Its old2015base was not mixed with the final same-base comparison. The archived later currenttable is also not the principal counterevidence.
